Verdict semantics: expected failures (author-flagged known deviations / non-deterministic cases) are reported as FAIL EXPECTED — genuine reds that are not hidden and must be explicitly accepted by the operator. A FAIL (or FAIL EXPECTED) accepted by the operator is reported as ACCEPTED FAIL with the mandatory justification and does not count against the overall verdict. Overall verdict is PASS only if no test case FAILs (or is left FAIL EXPECTED without acceptance) on any variant.

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_CmSlacParm_001

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_CmSlacParm_001.

Test objective: Test System executes GoodCase procedure, indicates the initial CP State B, waits for 5 % duty cycle and executes successful EIM process. Test System then checks that a nominal duty cycle can be detected after SUT changes CP State to E or F for T_step_EF. Furthermore a successful SLAC matching process shall be performed afterwards.

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_CmSlacParm_002

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_CmSlacParm_002.

Test objective: Test System executes GoodCase procedure, indicates the initial CP State B transition and waits for 5 % duty cycle fallback if the TT_EVSE_SLAC_init timer has expired and no CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ messages was sent before. Test System then counts the number of fallback sequences. Test System then checks that a 5 % duty cycle can be detected after SUT changes CP State to E or F for T_step_EF and whether this sequence is limited to 2 retries by the SUT. When the repetition limit is reached, the Test System checks if the SUT is initiating a oscillator shutdown.

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_PLCLinkStatus_006

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_PLCLinkStatus_006.

TC21_SECC_SDP_004

TC21_SECC_SDP_004.

Test objective: once the data link is established, send the default-parameter-set SDP request 50 times, each retransmission from a FRESH, distinct client UDP port drawn from the dynamic range (49152-65535), ignoring every response and always waiting the full SDP_Msg_Timeout (0.25 s) before switching to the next port -- the sequence never stops early. Passes if more than one SDP response is observed; each one is inherently addressed back to the exact client port its corresponding request was sent from (a UDP socket only ever receives datagrams sent to the port it is bound to), so counting responses across all per-request sockets already proves the per-request port match. Fewer than 50 responses, even though 50 requests are sent, is expected and acceptable given UDP's unreliable delivery.

Test case details — PIONIX interop testing (vendor-defined)

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_PionixInterop_005

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_PionixInterop_005.

Test objective: Interop; AC twin of the DC session-setup timing TC. The Test System runs a complete AC ISO 15118-2 session (eIM, TLS off) up to and including PowerDelivery(Start) and measures the EVSE response time of EVERY exchange before the ChargingStatus loop: supportedAppProtocol, SessionSetup, ServiceDiscovery, PaymentServiceSelection, Authorization, ChargeParameterDiscovery (AC energy transfer mode; no CableCheck/ PreCharge on AC) and PowerDelivery -- polled messages contribute one sample per poll. The measurement starts with the supportedAppProtocol handshake: the preceding SLAC matching is a precondition only and expressly NOT measured. Requests are timestamped at V2GTP frame send, responses at V2GTP frame arrival. Checks per message: the minimum shall be >= 90 ms (PIONIX interop requirement) and the maximum <= the standard's per-message limit V2G_SECC_Msg_Performance_Time (ISO 15118-2 Table 109: 1.5 s, resp. 4.5 s for PowerDeliveryRes). Per-message min/max are recorded; on failure every violating exchange is named exactly (message + sample number) with whether it came too quickly or took too long.

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_PionixInterop_006

TC_SECC_AC_VTB_PionixInterop_006.

Test objective: Interop; AC twin of the DC CurrentDemand-loop timing TC. The Test System runs a complete AC ISO 15118-2 charging session (eIM, plain TCP only: no-transport-security SDP request, the Test System never initiates TLS even on a TLS-capable DUT) into the AC charge loop (PowerDelivery(Start) done, contactors closed), then holds the loop for 10 minutes, sending a ChargingStatusReq (the AC analogue of CurrentDemandReq) every 250 ms. Every exchange is timestamped on the wire: request at V2GTP frame send, response at V2GTP frame arrival. Checks every ChargingStatusRes is OK, then the aggregate response times: the minimum shall be >= 90 ms and the maximum <= 120 ms (PIONIX interop requirement, not a normative ISO 15118 limit -- Table 109 would allow 1.5 s); the average is informational. The session is then ended cleanly (PowerDelivery(Stop), CP B, SessionStop(Terminate)), each with ResponseCode OK.
